chapter: Georgie Auld, Hawkins and Los Angeles
title: Conducting Auld's book and the Musicraft record
summary: He covers Auld's solo parts for a week, and recalls a record date after.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Yeah, a token of his appreciation. But he didn't know what I went through. I couldn't tell him, "Man, you upset me, because I really didn't know what charts was in the band." They might have had something in there I could play to feature me! But being it was his show, I said, "I'd better conduct it the way he's doing." So I had to take his solo parts. And I had to play them, because there was nobody else in the band could do it! He kind of left me hung up. But I sufficed for that week anyway.

And you know, Georgie came back the last day, then we came back to New York here, I think. And then I think that's when we went into the studio to make a record or something, that "Taps Miller" or something that we made.
Yeah. He recorded for Musicraft then.
Yeah, I think it was. I don't remember who it was for.
Yeah, I think they've been reissued. I have to check that out.
They recorded for Guild and for Musicraft, that band. Because Dizzy did that thing, "Co-Pilot" with him, but that was later. Of course, I remember Turk Van Lake was involved with it.
